$comment: SPEC §13.4.1 as data: what executing each §16 command can cause, by trigger. Read by
nbe-core's automation_effects.rs (preflight's static cycle check, SPEC §13.4) and by the
control plane's runtime check (automation.test.ts), which executes each command and asserts
the same-dispatch cells against what the evaluator actually raises. Prompt 11 WU5.
stateChange: the §13.2 stateChange FIELDS the command can change in its own dispatch (the
only fields a stateChange rule can name — nbe-core STATE_FIELDS; the control plane's
stateChanges() diffs exactly these). mediaStart: a take whose item goes on air, same dispatch
(B3). deferred: trigger kinds it can cause later, outside its dispatch — the cause chain does
not reach them, so the runtime suppression cannot see them; the static check does. item: the
payload key naming the ONE item whose mediaStart/mediaEnd the command can cause (absent: any).
note: a condition on a cell, named. A conditional write is still an edge: cycle detection asks what
a command CAN cause, not what it caused on one path. The two-key pass of 2026-09-29 found two edges
missing for exactly that reason (scene.arm, show.stop); the control plane's static-scan test now
set-compares every handler's writes against this file.

show.stop.note: streamState and recordState are set idle unconditionally (commands/show.ts); they change when an output was active

scene.arm.note: previewItem only when the preview is empty (state.ts armScene: previewItem == null -> previewItem = sceneId)

snapshot.recall.note: SPEC v0.4.8 row 1: the engine applies the recall as a cut through the take's application (directive.rs on_recall -> apply_take): the clip bus's source swaps (audioLevel, later) and the playback generation moves on, which runs the take's end scheduling. mediaEnd is over-approximated: no item is named in the payload (a snapshot is runtime state), so any item's end counts
